newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's WAPCO fortunes tumble mid-year.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's WAPCO fortunes tumble mid-year.

text.p: West African Portland Cement (WAPCO), Nigeria's leading cement company, on Tuesday posted mid-term after-tax profits to end-June 29 percent down at 850.3 million naira from 1,200 million naira in the same period last year.
Although turnover rose to 4.6 billion naira from 4.2 billion, pre-tax profit dropped 33 percent to 1.2 billion naira from 1.8 billion naira in the same period in 1995.
There was no official explanation for the decline.
"The company may be incurring higher costs of getting gypsum locally as its stockpile of the component diminishes," said one trader conversant with the building materials sector.
The Nigerian government last year banned importation of gypsum to compel cement companies to exploit local deposits in the north of the country.
Traders said while cement firms in north gained from their proximity to the gypsum sites WAPCO has had to pay higher to transport the item to its factory site in Western Nigeria.
Provision for taxation gulped 364.4 million naira against 647.6 million naira in 1995.
WAPCO shares, one of the blue chips on the Nigerian stock exchange, were unchanged at the end of trading on Tuesday at 38.15 naira. ($1=80 naira)
